question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the State shall work to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 46**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 46 of the Indian Constitution comes under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV).
 
• It mandates the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and other weaker sections of society.
 
• The provision emphasizes protecting these communities from social injustice and exploitation.
 
• The directive serves as a guiding principle for the government to formulate policies aimed at reducing inequalities and ensuring social justice.
 
• Though not legally enforceable, the principles under Part IV act as a moral obligation for the State.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• These are guidelines for the State to ensure socio-economic justice and aim to create a welfare state.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51) deals with the Directive Principles.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs):**
 
 
• SCs and STs are historically disadvantaged communities recognized in the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution provides special measures to uplift these groups, including reservations in education, employment, and political representation.
 
 
 
• **Social Justice and Equality:**
 
 
• Social justice refers to fair treatment and equal opportunities for all sections of society.
 
• Article 46 aligns with the broader goals of Articles 14 (Equality before the law) and 15 (Prohibition of discrimination).
 
 
 
• **Educational and Economic Measures:**
 
 
• Government schemes such as Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships, Eklavya Model Residential Schools, and Stand-Up India aim to empower SCs and STs.
 
• Skill development initiatives and financial inclusion programs are part of these efforts.
